# @zakkster/lite-charts

> Reactive, zero-GC chart library built on @zakkster/lite-scene. Signals
> for data, dimensions, theme, series visibility. v1.4.0 ships NINE
> chart types on FOUR independent kernels: line/area/bar/bubble/scatter
> on the axis kernel, pie/donut on the polar slice kernel, radar on
> its own kernel, and heatmap on its own grid kernel. Kernel boundaries
> are strict and verified with esbuild tree-shaking. line bundle ~40 KB
> minified, bar ~41 KB, bubble ~41 KB, scatter ~38 KB, pie ~22 KB,
> radar ~22 KB, heatmap ~22 KB. all-nine total: ~90 KB. Kernel-side
> auto-resize: omit width/height from config and the chart observes
> its mount container via ResizeObserver.
> v1.13.0 (current): overnight sessions + holiday calendar for
> createTimeLineChart shading. shading.sessions now accepts closeMinutes <
> openMinutes (overnight): the session splits at the UTC midnight seam into
> an evening half [open, 1440] on the original day mask and a morning half
> [0, close] on the mask rotated one weekday forward -- the single-cursor
> complement sweep is structurally unchanged and the seam never emits a band.
> `days` names the UTC weekday the session OPENS (a Mon-Fri overnight spec
> has morning halves Tue-Sat). closeMinutes === openMinutes still throws; a
> 24h session is {0, 1440}. NEW shading.holidays: number[] -- epoch-ms
> timestamps truncated to UTC day starts (Math.floor division; pre-1970
> floors correctly); each holiday closes its whole UTC day and FUSES with
> adjacent gap bands into one range. holidays without sessions synthesize a
> full-day Mon-Fri calendar internally (weekends + holidays), same
> validation. Fail-closed: [], null entries (null is not epoch 0),
> non-integers, strings, Date objects all throw at construction -- pass
> Date.UTC(...) values (new Date(y,m,d).getTime() is LOCAL midnight). No
> per-holiday fill (would break fusion); whole-UTC-day closure only (no
> early-close support). No-overnight/no-holiday specs produce band lists
> identical to v1.11.0-v1.12.0.
> v1.12.0: legend virtualization -- additive, opt-in, fully
> confined; a chart that does not set `legend.virtualize` is byte-unchanged
> (the eager `buildLegendDOM`..`installLegend` region is byte-identical,
> SHA-pinned by a test). `legend.virtualize: (host, opts) => ({ dispose })`
> hands the legend's row WINDOWING to a caller-supplied adapter -- wire it to
> @zakkster/lite-virtual's mountList (YOUR import; Charts.js contains ZERO
> references to lite-virtual, asserted by test; optional peerDep only,
> mirroring lite-delaunay's spatialIndex injection precedent). opts contract
> (allocated once per mount): { count, itemHeight, height, overscan,
> renderRow(rowEl, idx) }. The adapter owns row creation/position/height;
> Charts.js owns row CONTENTS: renderRow builds children once per pooled
> element, then on every (re)bind writes data-lc-idx, role/tabindex/
> aria-pressed, opacity, swatch colour, and label -- re-reading BOTH
> visibility (signal.peek(), untracked, no closure alloc) and colour per
> bind, so a recycled row never shows stale state. ONE shared visibility
> effect (subscribes to every seriesVisibility, repaints only bound rows via
> their own data-lc-idx) and ONE delegated click listener (dataset lookup,
> == null gated before unary +, integer + bounds checked) replace the eager
> path's per-row effect + per-row listener: exactly 4 disposers at any
> series count. Config: legend.height REQUIRED (int px > 0; null is not 0 --
> throws), itemHeight default 28, overscan default 2, position 'left'|'right'
> ONLY (top/bottom + virtualize throws; horizontal virtualization is a
> candidate). FAILS CLOSED at construction: non-function virtualize (false =
> absent = eager), bad height/itemHeight/overscan; at mount: a factory
> return without a dispose fn throws with NOTHING attached (chart.legend
> stays null). A11y: rows carry role="button"/tabindex/aria-pressed; focus
> does not survive scroll-out (pooled rows -- documented). 9 new tests
> (435->444): bounded 10..14-row window at 200 series, scroll rebind, the
> recycled-click signal-index bug, ASYMMETRIC-recycle dimmed state (a
> symmetric scroll-out/back cannot catch stale element state -- each slot
> returns to the same idx; proven by reversion), eager byte-identity +
> zero-reference confinement, validation matrix, handle validation, 50x
> mount/destroy retention, O(1) listeners at 20/200/2000 series. Torture A18:
> 50k-op scroll storm, chart-side 1.02 B/op vs 0.85 no-legend control (delta
> 0.17 <= 0.5), ZERO new signal-graph nodes (peek never subscribes), major
> GC 0.
> v1.11.0: market-hours session shading -- additive; one new config
> field + one new construction-time throw; every existing factory, the shared
> kernel, and the v1.10.0 weekend path byte-unchanged. createTimeLineChart's
> shading object gains sessions: [{openMinutes, closeMinutes, days?}] +
> sessionFill? -- UTC minutes-from-midnight (open 0..1439, close 1..1440,
> close > open), days = UTC weekday ints 0-6 defaulting Mon-Fri. Shades
> NON-trading time as the COMPLEMENT OF THE OPEN-INTERVAL UNION over the data
> extent: one range band per gap, Fri-close -> Mon-open is ONE contiguous band
> (sessions present => the weekend walker is never invoked -- weekends
> subsumed, nothing double-paints), multiple sessions/day (lunch-break
> markets) produce midday gap bands naturally. Implementation: cold
> `_normalizeSessionSpec` (construction-time validator -> {open, close,
> dayMask} sorted by open; dayMask bitfield, default 62 = Mon-Fri) +
> `_sessionBands` (single forward-only cursor sweep, NO sort at generation --
> ordering is an invariant of the validator sort + close<=1440; a comment
> marks that overnight support needs a real merge); `_shadingAnnotationsAcc`
> changed by exactly ONE generator-selection ternary; `_weekendBands` and the
> extent scan (raw accessor, per-row == null gate, SoA branch) byte-identical.
> Same cold/hot split as v1.10.0: bands generated in the annotation resolve,
> re-clipped per frame at 0 B. FAILS CLOSED at construction: null minute
> bounds (null is not midnight -- == null gated before any arithmetic),
> non-integers, out-of-range, zero-width, overnight close<open (throw names it
> unsupported), empty sessions/days, day ints outside 0..6; sessions:null =
> absent (weekend path). ALSO: explicit conflicting xScale.type now THROWS
> (previously silently forced 'time'); omitted/undefined/'time' unchanged;
> d.ts narrowed to Omit<XScaleConfig,'type'> & {type?:'time'}. Data-driven and
> TZ-agnostic: no exchange/timezone/holiday table; pre-convert local session
> times to UTC; overlay holidays via user annotations. Extent fully outside
> every session -> one full-extent band (documented). 8 new tests (427->435):
> exact 11-band canonical fixture (Mon-Fri 570/960 x 14 days), subsumption
> 11-vs-2, 21-band lunch-break, day masks, validator throw matrix, xScale
> throw, per-row null-x reuse, tree-shake confinement (1 immediate-paren
> call-site each), retention, exact-bounds union invariants for contained/
> overlapping/back-to-back sets -- TS18 + TS22 proven load-bearing by
> reversion (TS22 strengthened from count-only to exact from/to lists after a
> cursor-regression reversion stayed green). torture ok (A17: 1.065 B/op vs
> 0.861 weekend control, delta 0.204, 44 bands). ASCII clean. Composition
> recipe (README): a lite-time clock(60000) read inside the annotations
> accessor gives a self-advancing now-line; bands + now-line re-derive per
> beat on the cold path, draw stays 0 B.
> v1.10.0: createTimeLineChart + weekend shading -- additive; a new
> factory and a new config field, every existing factory + the shared kernel
> byte-unchanged. createTimeLineChart(config) is createLineChart with three
> time-first defaults: (1) xScale.type forced to 'time' regardless of the x key
> or data probe (inferXScaleType only infers time for a Date probe or a
> {time,date,t} key >= 1e11, so a plain numeric x key would render linear);
> (2) panBounds defaults to 'data' so the reachable view equals the data domain;
> (3) an optional shading config (true | 'weekends' | {fill?}) adds one weekend
> band per Sat 00:00 -> Mon 00:00 UTC span in the data domain. Bands are plain
> {type:'range',axis:'x',from,to,fill} rows riding the v1.7.0 annotation layer:
> generated COLD inside the annotation resolve effect, re-clipped each frame by
> the existing project effect at 0 B (no new draw-path code), composing with any
> user annotations (bands first) and exported by exportSVG. The extent is derived
> from the series DATA accessors (epoch ms, UTC), NEVER xScale.dMin/dMax -- the
> annotation resolve effect tracks themeVersion + the annotations accessor but
> not scaleVersion, so reading the scale would re-allocate bands every pan/zoom
> frame; reading the data regenerates them only on data change. _weekendBands +
> _shadingAnnotationsAcc are referenced ONLY from createTimeLineChart (tree-shake
> out of a createLineChart-only bundle). FAILS CLOSED: a null extent bound is
> gated (== null) before any unary + so it becomes NaN not epoch 0 (+null===0);
> a non-finite/inverted extent emits no bands; the scan reads x through a RAW
> accessor and gates each ROW == null before coercion, so one {x:null} row
> cannot collapse the extent to 1970 (NaN garbage self-skips; Date x maps via
> getTime()); SoA {xs,ys} data is scanned like AoS (an Array.isArray-only gate
> silently unshaded it -- caught in review); shading:false is a first-class
> opt-out (behaves like absent, matching the boolean type); other invalid
> shading values throw at construction. Timezone-agnostic (epoch ms in; caller
> formats). Market-hours / session calendars out of scope (v1.10.x).
> 14 new tests (413->427): weekend-walk boundaries, null/non-finite/inverted
> fail-close, no-shading passthrough, band+user composition, SoA regression,
> forced time scale, annotation-count integration, opt-in null handle, config
> validation, tree-shake source confinement, retention, false opt-out, row-level
> null guard -- TS2 (null-gate), TS5 (SoA), TS13 (false opt-out), TS14 (row null)
> proven load-bearing by reversion. torture ok (A16 0-B weekend-shading redraw
> storm), ASCII clean.
> v1.9.0: horizontal-bar brush -- additive; completes the horizontal
> interaction set (the slice deferred from v1.8.0). createBarChart({
> orientation:'horizontal', brush:true}) selects on shift-drag a value range
> (screen-X, the value axis under the swap, via yScale.invert) crossed with a
> band set (screen-Y, via xScale.invert -> band index). It emits a DISTINCT
> payload {valueMin, valueMax, bandMin, bandMax, bands, ids} (bands = category
> keys; ids = primary-series rows) -- the vertical/line/scatter brush keeps
> {xMin, xMax, yMin, yMax, ids}. Built as a swapAxes ? <remapped> : <current>
> selection at each brush call site (_commitBrush, drawBrushOverlay,
> brushFacade.set); the pure helpers _normalizeBrushRect / _brushPxToData /
> _computeBrushIds / makeBandScale stay BYTE-IDENTICAL -- _computeBrushIds
> applies unchanged because a bar stores its band index in state.xs and value in
> state.ys. The overlay rect spans xScale.leftEdge(bandMin)..leftEdge(bandMax)+
> bandWidth (band edges, not centers); per-frame draw 0 B, commit allocates at
> gesture rate only. FAILS CLOSED: an empty-category chart (xScale.invert -> -1)
> commits null (never bands:[undefined]); setBrush forces a null bound to NaN
> before Number.isFinite (a null value bound is NOT coerced to 0); horizontal +
> a log value axis still throws at construction, checked before brush. 7 new
> tests (406->413): value-range+band-set mapping, full-plot select, click-clear,
> facade validation, vertical-brush regression guard, band-edge overlay
> alignment, empty-category fail-close -- HB1/HB3/HB5/HB7 proven load-bearing by
> measured reversion. torture ok (0-B overlay storm, A15), ASCII clean.
> v1.8.0: horizontal-bar interactions -- additive, no public API
> change beyond enabling existing flags on a new orientation.
> createBarChart({orientation:'horizontal'}) now accepts pan, zoom, and a value
> grid. Under the axis-role swap the VALUE axis is on screen-X (bound via
> yScale) and the BAND axis on screen-Y, so a horizontal drag pans the value
> domain and the wheel zooms it around the cursor value; the band axis stays
> pinned. view.yMin/view.yMax address the value axis (the x fields hold the band
> domain and pan/zoom as an identity). Built by remapping the linear kernels at
> each gesture boundary: onPanMove uses swapAxes ? _applyPan(view,0,-dx,w,w),
> onWheel uses swapAxes ? _applyZoom(...,pb.w-(p.x-pb.x),...,1,zoomFactor) with
> proposedXRatio forced to 1; _applyPan/_applyZoom/_clampToBounds stay
> BYTE-IDENTICAL (swapAxes is true only for BAR_RENDERER) and the vertical path
> is unchanged. buildGrid gained one swapAxes option (default false, single
> shared call site) that flips value gridlines to vertical. Per-frame draw stays
> 0 B. FAILS CLOSED: horizontal + brush (a value-range + band-ids payload is a
> separate future cut) and horizontal + a log value axis throw at construction,
> before any signal alloc. 6 new tests (400->406): value-axis pan (a horizontal
> drag translates the value scale by exactly dx px), vertical-drag control (no
> value move), cursor-anchored zoom (value under cursor stable to 1e-9), vertical
> value grid, fail-closed throws, mount/pan/destroy retention -- each proven
> load-bearing by measured reversion. torture ok (new horizontal-interaction 0-B
> case), ASCII clean.
> v1.7.0: annotation layer -- additive, no public API change beyond
> the new config. annotations: Annotation[] | (() => Annotation[]) on any
> axis-kernel chart (line/area/bar/bubble/scatter). Four shapes: line
> {axis:'x'|'y', value, color?, dash?, width?, label?} (a rule at a data value);
> range {axis:'x'|'y', from, to, fill?, label?} (a shaded band); point {x, y,
> color?, radius?, label?}; text {x, y, text, color?, anchor?:'start'|'middle'|
> 'end'}. Marks pin to DATA coords and re-project through the live xScale/yScale
> every scale change, so they track pan/zoom and log axes; a value that maps
> off-scale (log value<=0, or panned out) is clipped to the plot rect (not
> painted over axes). Rendered ABOVE the series and BELOW the crosshair/brush
> (annGroup added to scene.root between the series loop and the crosshair node);
> emitted by exportSVG (native lineNode/textNode + a pathNode for fills/markers).
> ZERO per-frame alloc: a two-step design -- a COLD resolve step (tracks a theme
> signal + the annotations accessor) sizes pooled nodes and resolves --css-var
> colors via getComputedStyle; a HOT project step (tracks scaleVersion +
> plotBoundsSignal, runs every pan frame) writes pooled-node underscore fields
> DIRECTLY (no node.set, no literals, no resolveColor) and markDirty once.
> FAILS CLOSED: a non-finite value/from/to/x/y (null/undefined/NaN) draws
> nothing (Number.isFinite, never Number(null)===0 at data-zero); unknown type
> ignored. Theme-aware: --css-var color/fill re-resolve on refreshTheme (bumps
> the cold theme signal). Runtime-isolated: no annotations config => null handle,
> no scene child, buildAnnotations gated behind if(annotationsAcc) (statically
> reachable like buildGrid, so no bundler drop -- gated at runtime, not tree-
> shaken). Swap-aware: axis names the DATA axis; on orientation:'horizontal' the
> value axis is on screen-X so an axis:'y' rule draws as a vertical screen line.
> 10 new tests (390->400): projection, pan-clip, reactive range via signal,
> exportSVG parity, theme re-resolve (+ resolveColor off the redraw path), log
> AND linear fail-closed (linear is the load-bearing one -- log masks
> Number(null)===0 since map(0) is non-finite), runtime isolation, horizontal-bar
> swap, pool retention/high-water. torture ok (new 0-B/frame annotation case),
> ASCII clean.
> v1.6.1: mixed-sign log-domain floor -- a correctness patch, no
> public API change. A type:'log' domain spanning zero (min<=0, max>0) drew
> correctly but NaN'd the view on the FIRST pan/zoom: the reactive scale effect
> floored the domain to its positive part for RENDER (local xlo/xhi, lo/hi) but
> wrote the RAW (<=0) min into _dataDomain, so the gesture math (_clampToBoundsLog,
> axisSpan) took log() of a value <=0. FIX: floor _dataDomain.xMin/.yMin to the
> same positive part (dxMax*1e-9 / yBase[1]*1e-9) using the SAME >0 predicate as
> the render floor, computed from the DATA extent (not the view-overridden
> xLo/yLo), only when that axis is log AND has a positive extent. Two cold ifs in
> the scale effect; per-frame draw byte-unchanged; linear/time path only gains
> never-taken branches. FAILS CLOSED preserved: a log domain with NO positive
> extent still throws at MOUNT (the floor cannot mask it -- the throw is upstream
> and fires first). Symmetric on x and y. 7 new tests (383->390): y-pan, x/y
> positive-domain regression (exact-clamp, not floored), x/y no-positive-extent
> throw, x/y zoom-path; the pre-existing x-pan characterization test was
> reconciled to assert the finite (moved, min>0) view. torture ok, ASCII clean.
> v1.6.0: x-axis log scale. additive, no public API change beyond
> enabling the config. xScale:{type:'log'} now works on the CONTINUOUS
> axis-kernel charts (line/area/scatter/bubble; NOT bar -- band x is not
> continuous). base-10 log, decade ticks via lite-axis.logTicks, map(x<=0)=NaN
> (segments break, markers skip), and log-space pan/zoom -- symmetric with the
> y-axis log that shipped in v1.4.0. the interaction helpers (_applyPanLog/
> _applyZoomLog/_clampToBoundsLog) already took an xLog flag; point projection
> was made x-log-aware in the v1.5.1 patch; so v1.6.0 is mostly construction +
> the reactive domain wiring. FAILS CLOSED: a log x-domain with no positive
> extent throws at MOUNT naming the domain (mirrors the y _logDomainError path,
> leaks no signal); xScale:{type:'log'} + a categorical (bar/band) or time
> x-axis throws at CONSTRUCTION before any signal alloc (a scale is one type).
> the common linear-x path is byte-unchanged (one cold if in the scale effect).
> 15 new tests (368->383); T6.A13 torture gate extended with an xLog-only
> projection body (<=16 B/op abs, <=2.0 B/op vs linear-x, maxMajor:0). KNOWN at
> ship (FIXED in v1.6.1 above): a mixed-sign log domain (min<=0,max>0) floored to
> positive for render but left _dataDomain min unfloored, so the first gesture
> NaN'd the view (fail-closed); identical on y; v1.6.1 floors both axes together.
> v1.5.1: a correctness patch, no public API change. Fixes
> log-scale point projection. scaleSeriesToPixels -- the per-extract hot loop
> that maps domain values to pixels for every projectToPixels renderer
> (line/area/scatter/bubble) -- inlined linear v*slope+intercept for both
> axes; on a yScale:{type:'log'} chart the log-space slope hit the raw value
> without log() first, so the axis+ticks were correct but every point landed
> off-canvas (top decade of a [1,1000] domain ~tens of thousands of px above a
> 400px canvas). Present since y-log shipped in v1.4.1. Fix: xLog/yLog resolved
> once above the loop, four cold-selected flat bodies (linear/linear, log-x,
> log-y, log-both); a log axis applies v>0 ? log(v)*slope+intercept : NaN so
> non-positive samples break the polyline exactly as map() does; no per-point
> branch, no allocation; the linear/linear body is byte-identical (12k-point
> Object.is parity gate). Bars unaffected (BAR_RENDERER projectToPixels:false).
> xScale:{type:'log'} still threw at construction as of 1.5.1 (x-log was a
> separate feature, wired in v1.6.0 above). Torture gate T6.A13 bounds the log
> branch at maxMajor:0, <=2.0 B/op vs the identical linear projection.
> v1.5.0: a presentation cut, additive over v1.4.1, both opt-in,
> no public API breaks. (1) createDonutChart `centerLabel` -- a number in
> the donut hole as a pointer-events:none DOM overlay (NOT canvas text),
> font owned by CSS `clamp(--cl-min, calc(--cl-fit / --cl-digits),
> --cl-max)`; chart writes hole radius + label digit-count as custom props
> on data/resize only (sub-Hz), zero per-frame JS, no measureText; box
> constrained to the hole's inscribed square; fail-closed (throws on a pie
> or innerRadius-0 hole, and minFontSize > maxFontSize); exportSVG emits an
> equivalent centered <text>, exportPNG does NOT include the overlay.
> (2) createBarChart `orientation: 'horizontal'` -- category band on the Y
> axis (category 0 at top), bars grow from the value baseline along X;
> vertical draw path is byte-identical (peer draw fn + pixel-range swap
> chosen once at setup, no per-frame branch); fail-closed subset -- throws
> when combined with pan/zoom/brush/value-grid/log axis (deferred to a
> later 1.5.x); crosshair().snapPixelX is the band-axis pixel when
> horizontal. See the dedicated sections below for both.
> v1.4.0: the v1.4 release. THREE new interaction primitives
> on axis-kernel charts plus FOUR pre-existing allocation traps closed
> during a bare-metal audit. No public API breaks vs v1.3.0; all new
> features are opt-in. (1) Log scale on the y-axis via
> `yScale: { type: 'log' }` -- base-10 log on any axis-kernel chart;
> ticks via `lite-axis.logTicks` (decade boundaries); polymorphic
> s.map() handles linear and log without parallel code paths; map(v<=0)
> returns NaN so line/area break segments and markers skip; updateLogScale
> FAILS CLOSED on a non-positive/collapsed domain (v1.4.1 C0/LC-04 -- throws,
> naming the bound, no more 1e-10 substitution). (2) Pan + zoom via
> `pan: true` / `zoom: true` -- pointer-drag pans (cursor-anchor
> convention: data point under cursor stays under cursor as it moves,
> drag right -> view shifts LEFT in data space, drag up -> view shifts
> DOWN); wheel zooms around cursor; `chart.view` reactive facade
> (callable for tracked read, .peek for untracked, .set / .reset);
> imperative aliases setView/resetView; view shape
> { xMin, xMax, yMin, yMax } each nullable for "fall back to data
> domain on that axis" -- shape INTENTIONALLY symmetric with
> lite-camera-max's camera signal for future lite-gl drop-in;
> panBounds: 'data' | 'free' (default 'data' clamps); zoomMin/zoomMax
> as visible-span/data-span ratios; zoomStep wheel ratio (default
> 1.15). (3) Brushing via `brush: true` -- shift+drag rectangle
> selects; chart.brush emits BrushSelection
> { xMin, xMax, yMin, yMax, ids } where ids are indices into the
> primary series (freshly allocated per gesture commit, gesture-driven
> only -- programmatic setBrush leaves ids as null); modifier routing
> ensures all three interactions coexist on the same canvas (bare drag
> = pan, shift+drag = brush, wheel = zoom); click-to-clear at 3px
> threshold matches d3-brush; live updates per pointermove so
> cross-chart linking via effect() reflects the drag in real time;
> translucent rect overlay drawn after the crosshair node so it sits
> on top; brushStyle: { fill, stroke, lineDash, lineWidth } overrides.
> All three feature blocks share the same opt-in pattern: setting any
> of pan/zoom/brush to true allocates the listener cluster, otherwise
> zero cost. (4) Four allocation traps closed (the audit): heatmap
> quantile Float32Array pool replacing const-present-array +
> push().sort(cmp); _parseRGBLike indexOf scan replacing per-cell
> split(','); charBufToString via String.fromCharCode.apply replacing
> rope-string loop; SVG-export path chunks (array + join once)
> replacing this._currentPath += chunk (this was the consequential
> fix -- pre-fix, 100k+ point exports could hit V8's max rope length
> and throw RangeError or stall the main thread for seconds; post-fix,
> 50k-point scatter exports a 5.2 MB SVG in 165 ms with no issues).
> No public API changes from the audit; pre-existing leaks in v1.2-1.3
> code, fixed silently. Tests: 320 (vs v1.3.0's 259, +61 across the
> alpha line). Bundles vs v1.3.0: axis-kernel charts +7.4 KB each
> (~0.7 log, ~0.1 audit, ~3.7 pan/zoom, ~2.9 brush); heatmap +0.4 KB
> (audit fix's presentSorted field); pie/donut/radar +0.2 KB (shared
> module-level code touched). All-nine: 82.4 -> 90.2 KB. Bench
> unchanged through the entire alpha line (161-167 bytes/cycle noise
> band, same as v1.3.0's 161). Bar inherits typing for
> pan/zoom/brush but band x-axis isn't ideal for panning -- not
> documented as supported in v1.4. Polar/radar/heatmap don't get the
> interaction primitives (different interaction models). Log + pan/zoom
> is LOG-AWARE as of v1.4.1 (C0): _applyPanLog/_applyZoomLog work in
> log space (drag d px on n-decade axis multiplies bounds by 10^(n*d/H)),
> per-axis branching, a log floor stops drift to 0/Infinity; the same log-space
> pan/zoom applies to x-log as of v1.6.0. Linear path is byte-identical
> (parity-tested). Forward plan: the
> view-signal shape was chosen specifically to drop unchanged into a
> future @zakkster/lite-charts-gl companion package (separate npm
> package on @zakkster/lite-gl); that work is post-v1.4. See README
> for the per-feature usage guides, ROADMAP for the longer arc.
> v1.4.0-alpha.3: brushing -- final v1.4 alpha. Opt in via
> brush: true on any axis-kernel chart. Shift+drag selects a
> rectangular region; chart emits BrushSelection { xMin, xMax, yMin,
> yMax, ids } via chart.brush reactive facade. Same pattern as
> chart.view: chart.brush() reads (tracks in effects), .peek() reads
> untracked, .set(v) writes, .clear() clears; chart.setBrush(v) and
> chart.clearBrush() are imperative aliases. Both throw if `brush:
> true` was not in config. ids are indices into the PRIMARY series
> (first series in series[], or the single-series data); freshly
> allocated each gesture commit (not pooled -- aliasing across
> brushes would surprise users; brushing is sub-Hz so the allocation
> is acceptable). Programmatic setBrush() leaves ids as null unless
> the caller passes them -- the API never recomputes ids on imperative
> set; only gesture-driven brushes populate ids. Modifier routing:
> bare drag = pan (when pan: true), shift+drag = brush (when
> brush: true), wheel = zoom (when zoom: true, modifier-agnostic).
> Pointerdown checks ev.shiftKey and the pan listener returns early
> when shift is held AND brush is enabled, so the same canvas can host
> all three interactions without conflict. Click-to-clear: shift+click
> with total drag distance under 3 px is treated as a click and clears
> the existing brush (matches d3-brush). Live updates: brushSig
> updates on every pointermove during gesture -- cross-chart linking
> via effect() reflects the user's drag in real time. Visual: a
> translucent rect overlay rendered AFTER the crosshair node so it
> sits on top. Defaults to indigo accent fill (rgba(99, 102, 241,
> 0.15)) + dashed accent outline ([4, 4], 1px). Override via
> brushStyle: { fill, stroke, lineDash, lineWidth }; pass lineDash: []
> for solid outline. Math helpers: _normalizeBrushRect(px0, py0, px1,
> py1) orders a drag rect into min/max corners; _brushPxToData(rect,
> xScale, yScale) inverts pixel rect to data bounds via scales
> (y-flipped: pyMin -> yMax, pyMax -> yMin); _computeBrushIds(xs, ys,
> n, xMin, xMax, yMin, yMax) returns array of indices inside the
> rect. All three pure module-level, exported via _testHelpers for
> white-box tests, tree-shaken away in builds that don't use brush
> (only reachable through listener closures, only built when brush
> enabled). Types: BrushSelection, BrushStyleConfig, BrushConfig
> interfaces added; Chart interface gains brush, setBrush, clearBrush;
> LineChartConfig, BubbleChartConfig, ScatterChartConfig extend
> BrushConfig (bar inherits via existing Omit chain). Scope: axis-
> kernel charts only -- polar/radar/heatmap don't get brushing
> (different interaction models). 320/320 tests pass.
> Bundles: line +2.9 KB, bar +2.9 KB, bubble +2.8 KB, scatter +2.9 KB
> vs alpha.2; heatmap/pie/radar UNCHANGED (kernel isolation verified --
> no brush strings in those bundles). All-nine: 87.3 -> 90.2 KB. Bench
> unchanged (164.0 vs alpha.2's 164.7 -- noise band). v1.4.0 combined
> release follows next -- same code as alpha.3 plus a clean release-
> notes rollup, no further API or behavior changes.
> v1.4.0-alpha.2: pan + zoom land on axis-kernel charts.
> Opt in via pan: true and/or zoom: true (defaults false). Either flag
> allocates the view signal and attaches the listener cluster; neither
> set = no view, no listeners, zero cost. Cursor-anchor convention
> throughout (d3-zoom / Plotly / Google Maps): the data point under
> the cursor at gesture start stays under the cursor as it moves.
> Drag right -> view shifts left in data space (xMin decreases); drag
> up -> view shifts down in data space (yMin decreases, content rolls
> up with the cursor, y-axis labels effectively scroll down). Wheel
> up zooms in, wheel down zooms out; each tick scales by zoomStep
> (default 1.15). Pan uses pointer events uniformly so pen, touch,
> and mouse all work; setPointerCapture is used when available so a
> drag that escapes the canvas still completes. Wheel listener
> registered with passive: false + preventDefault so page-scroll
> doesn't fight the zoom. chart.view is a reactive facade mirroring
> chart.crosshair: chart.view() reads (tracks in effects), .peek()
> reads untracked, .set(v) writes a view object
> ({ xMin, xMax, yMin, yMax } with any field nullable to fall back to
> data domain), .reset() clears back to null. chart.setView and
> chart.resetView are imperative aliases. Both throw if neither pan
> nor zoom was set (signals the opt-in requirement). View shape is
> intentionally symmetric with lite-camera-max's camera signal so the
> same value drops into a future lite-gl project() function unchanged
> when @zakkster/lite-charts-gl lands. Bounds policy via panBounds:
> 'data' (default) clamps to data domain (zoom-out wider than data
> snaps to full domain); panBounds: 'free' allows any view (extend
> past data, useful for context space). zoomMin/zoomMax express the
> visible-span/data-span ratio (defaults 0.01 / 1000). Architecture:
> view-override layer sits between data-domain extraction and the
> scale-update calls -- the scale-update effect adds viewSig() as a
> dependency so chart.setView() triggers full re-project + redraw via
> existing reactive plumbing; no parallel code path. _dataDomain is a
> plain object (non-reactive) snapshot populated by the scale-update
> effect, read by listeners inside event handlers for bounds clamping
> without touching the reactive graph. Math helpers (_applyPan,
> _applyZoom, _clampToBounds) are module-level + pure, exported via
> _testHelpers for white-box unit tests, dropped by tree-shaking in
> builds that don't use pan/zoom (they reach the chart only through
> listener closures, only constructed when interactionsEnabled).
> Scope: axis-kernel charts (line/area/bubble/scatter typed via
> LineChartConfig extends PanZoomConfig). Bar inherits typing via
> Omit<LineChartConfig,...> but band x-axis isn't ideal for panning;
> not documented as supported. Log-aware as of v1.4.1 (C0): _applyPanLog/
> _applyZoomLog work in log space per-axis (linear path byte-identical),
> with a floor that keeps a free pan from drifting the domain to 0/Inf;
> x-log is supported as of v1.6.0 (same log-space math). Polar/radar/heatmap
> kernels don't get pan/zoom.
> Brushing (originally alpha.2) shifts to alpha.3: modifier-key drag
> emits brushSignal for cross-chart filtering; will coexist with
> pan/zoom (no modifier = pan, shift = brush). 304/304 tests pass.
> v1.4.0-alpha.1: audit-fix-only release. Four allocation traps
> traps inherited from v1.2-1.3 code, surfaced in a bare-metal review:
> (1) heatmap quantile gather/sort was `const present = []; .push();
> .sort(cmp)` -- on a 200x200 dense heatmap that's a 40k-element JS
> Array allocated per data update. Fixed: pool a Float32Array on
> state.presentSorted, pack values into a prefix, sort an in-place
> subarray(0, n) view via Float32Array.prototype.sort() (no comparator,
> sorts numerically and allocates nothing). (2) heatmap _parseRGBLike
> called `css.slice(open+1,close).split(',')` per cell at extract --
> 10k cells = 10k Arrays + 30k substrings. Fixed: indexOf scan with
> three substring slices total. (3) charBufToString built its result
> by `s += String.fromCharCode(buf[i])` in a loop, allocating N
> intermediate strings via V8's rope walk -- ~200 allocations per
> axis update. Fixed: String.fromCharCode.apply(null, buf.subarray(0,
> n)), one call, one allocation. (4) the SVG-export shim accumulated
> path commands by `this._currentPath += chunk` for every moveTo /
> lineTo / etc. -- at 100k+ points this could hit V8's max rope
> length and throw RangeError, or stall the main thread for seconds
> during the rope flatten in stroke()/fill(). Fixed: array-of-chunks,
> every path command pushes into this._pathChunks, stroke/fill/clip
> joins exactly once via this._pathD(). beginPath truncates the array
> by length=0 (no realloc); fillRect/strokeRect rotated-fallback swaps
> chunks arrays. Verified: 50,000-point scatter chart now exports to
> a 5.2 MB SVG with 50,021 path elements in 165ms (pre-alpha.1 this
> would have either crashed or stalled). No public API changes. The
> v1.4 interaction-primitives work (pan + zoom, brushing) shifts one
> alpha slot forward: alpha.2 = pan/zoom, alpha.3 = brushing.
> 280/280 tests pass.
> v1.4.0-alpha.0: log scale on the y-axis. Opt in with
> yScale: { type: 'log' } on any axis-kernel chart (line, area, bar,
> bubble, scatter). NEW makeLogScale() + updateLogScale(s, dMin,
> dMax, rMin, rMax) -- same shape as makeLinearScale but map(v) does
> Math.log(v) * slope + intercept and invert(px) does Math.exp((px -
> intercept) * invSlope). Tick generation routes through lite-axis's
> already-shipped logTicks (decade boundaries 1, 10, 100, ...; major-
> only for alpha.0, the minor 2x/5x sub-tick mode is parked for a
> later cut). map(v <= 0) returns NaN explicitly so draw fns can
> break the segment (line/area) or skip the marker (bubble/scatter).
> updateLogScale safety-clamps non-positive dMin to 1e-10 so a
> degenerate domain doesn't break the chart. Polymorphic s.map() in
> tick projection (was inlined slope-intercept) handles linear and
> log without parallel code paths -- ~12 method calls per axis update,
> sub-Hz rate, perf-irrelevant. v1.4 alpha line continues: alpha.1
> pan + zoom (view signal symmetric with lite-camera-max), alpha.2
> brushing (modifier-key drag emits brushSignal for cross-chart
> filtering). 272/272 tests pass.
> v1.3.0: chart.exportSVG() across all four kernels. NEW
> chart.exportSVG(opts?) returns a complete <svg>...</svg> string
> with xmlns, viewBox, width, height -- droppable into HTML pages,
> PDFs, image-converter pipelines, or diffable test fixtures.
> Implementation: a Canvas2D-shaped shim (_SVGRenderingContext2D,
> ~270 LOC) accumulates SVG markup instead of issuing pixel ops; the
> _drawNodeToSVG walker recursively traverses scene.root through it,
> structurally mirroring lite-scene's drawNode/drawSelf so every node
> kind (rect, circle, line, text, path, group with clip) is covered.
> The chart's draw callbacks don't know they're rendering to SVG --
> they call the canvas API as always. Geometric output is identical
> to canvas paint (minus DPR scaling -- SVG is resolution-
> independent). SVGExportOptions: { background?: string | null } --
> defaults to the chart's construction-time background. The chart
> must be mounted; mock canvases work (SVG export doesn't read pixel
> data). Text-width estimation is approximate (~0.55 em per char).
> Bar category-label centering bug fixed: pre-existing typo
> (anchor: 'center' instead of align: 'center') at Charts.js line
> 1329 had been silently offsetting multi-character labels right by
> half a glyph width. Both canvas and SVG benefit.
> v1.2.0: chart.destroy() across all four kernels + heatmap polish
> (row+column highlights, quantile color binning, auto-contrast value
> labels). v1.2.0-alpha.3: createHeatmap on the new grid kernel.
> v1.2.0-alpha.2: multi-series bubble + per-point color + global
> size domain. v1.2.0-alpha.1: createScatterChart. v1.2.0-alpha.0:
> spatial-index foundation. v1.1.0: bar layout polish. 259/259
> tests pass.
> ESM-only. Single-file ~6.9k lines. Four peer deps (lite-signal,
> lite-scene, lite-axis required; lite-delaunay optional), zero
> runtime deps. MIT.
> See ROADMAP.md for forward plan: v1.4 log scale + pan/zoom +
> brushing, v1.5 time-series specialized variants + annotations.

## Why use this library

- You need a chart that re-renders automatically when a signal changes
  (data, width, theme, etc.) without manual `.update()` calls.
- You're streaming live data (100-100k points/sec) and Chart.js drops frames.
- You're in a Twitch Extension or game HUD with a 1 MB / 60 fps budget that
  rules out Chart.js (~78 KB) or D3 (~70+ KB plus selection allocation).
- You want a Vega-Lite middle ground: sensible defaults + escape hatches.

## When NOT to use

- You need SVG output -- coming v1.3. Today only `exportPNG`.
- You need server-side rendering -- the renderer is Canvas2D-bound.
- You need `<200` points across one chart and don't care about GC --
  Chart.js is simpler and the bundle-size argument is weaker at that
  scale.
- You need built-in heatmap, scatter, or polar-area charts today -- on
  the roadmap (v1.2.0 +) but not yet shipped.

## Module shape

ESM-only. Named exports from the single `Charts.js` entry:

```ts
function createLineChart(config: LineChartConfig): Chart;
function createAreaChart(config: AreaChartConfig): Chart;
function createBarChart(config: BarChartConfig): Chart;
function createBubbleChart(config: BubbleChartConfig): Chart;
function createScatterChart(config: ScatterChartConfig): Chart;
function createPieChart(config: PieChartConfig): Chart;
function createDonutChart(config: DonutChartConfig): Chart;
function createRadarChart(config: RadarChartConfig): Chart;
function createHeatmap(config: HeatmapConfig): Chart;

// Public interface for the spatial-index integration (v1.2.0-alpha.0+).
interface SpatialIndex {
    findNearest(qx, qy, k, maxDistSq, outIndices, outDistSq): number;
    dispose(): void;
}
type SpatialIndexFactory = (pxs, pys, n) => SpatialIndex;
```

Nine chart types across four strictly-independent kernels.

`AreaChartConfig extends LineChartConfig` with three additional fields:

```ts
interface AreaChartConfig extends LineChartConfig {
    baseline?: number | 'bottom';   // default 0; 'bottom' = bottom of plot rect
    stroke?: boolean;               // default true; whether to stroke upper boundary
    fillOpacity?: number;           // default 0.3; multiplied into globalAlpha for fill
}
```

`BarChartConfig` is line config minus interpolation/markers (don't apply
to bars), plus bar-specific layout:

```ts
interface BarChartConfig extends Omit<LineChartConfig, 'interpolation' | 'markers' | 'xScale'> {
    baseline?: number;        // default 0; where bars anchor on the y-axis
    paddingInner?: number;    // default 0.15; gap between bands as fraction of step
    paddingOuter?: number;    // default 0.1;  padding at each end of the range
    groupInnerPad?: number;   // default 0.08; gap between bars within a grouped slot
    xScale?: { domain?: string[] };   // explicit categories if needed
}
```

Bar charts treat x as a categorical key. Data shape: `[{x: 'Q1', y: 42}, ...]`.
String, number, or any value that survives `String(x)` round-trip works.
Multi-series renders **grouped** side-by-side; each bar occupies a slice of
the band centered on its series index. The y-domain always includes the
`baseline` (default 0) so bars don't visually float.

Hit detection is discrete and O(1): `Math.floor((px - origin) / step)`.
No bisection -- the discriminator is categorical. The crosshair snaps to
the nearest band; per-series markers are skipped (bars highlight
themselves).

## Core types

```ts
interface LineChartConfig {
    // Data shape: either `data` (single series shorthand) or `series`.
    data?: Row[] | (() => Row[]) | { xs: Float32Array; ys: Float32Array };
    series?: SeriesConfig[];

    // Accessors. String key, integer index, or function. Default 'x' / 'y'.
    x?: string | number | ((row: any, i: number) => number);
    y?: string | number | ((row: any, i: number) => number);

    // Static-or-signal dimensions.
    width?: number | (() => number);
    height?: number | (() => number);

    margin?: { top?: number; right?: number; bottom?: number; left?: number };

    // Style. CSS color strings (hex/rgb/oklch/named) or "--css-var" tokens
    // resolved against the container via getComputedStyle at mount time.
    color?: string;
    lineWidth?: number;
    background?: string | null;
    axisColor?: string;
    labelColor?: string;
    font?: string;

    // Device pixel ratio override. Default: globalThis.devicePixelRatio.
    dpr?: number;

    // Scale overrides. Without these, x-type is inferred from the first
    // data row (Date probe -> time; numeric -> linear) and y-domain is
    // computed from union of all series with 5% nice padding.
    xScale?: { type?: 'linear' | 'time'; domain?: [number, number] };
    yScale?: { domain?: [number, number]; zero?: boolean; nice?: boolean };

    // Crosshair: vertical line + per-series marker dots at the snapped x.
    // Default true. `crosshair: false` disables the line + markers but keeps
    // the tooltip if it's also enabled.
    crosshair?: boolean | { color?: string; dash?: number[] };

    // Tooltip: canvas-drawn box at the snapped x. Default true. `format`
    // receives `{snapIdx, snapDomainX, xScaleType, rows}` and may return a
    // string (header-only, suppresses rows) or `{header?, rows?}`.
    tooltip?: boolean | {
        background?: string;
        border?: string;
        format?: (ctx: {
            snapIdx: number;
            snapDomainX: number;
            xScaleType: 'linear' | 'time';
            rows: Array<{ color: string; label: string; value: string }>;
        }) => string | { header?: string; rows?: any[] };
    };

    // Legend: DOM-rendered with click-to-toggle visibility. Default 'bottom'.
    // Auto-wraps the canvas in a flex container; pass `legend.container` to
    // append into an existing element instead.
    legend?: boolean | 'top' | 'bottom' | 'left' | 'right' | {
        position?: 'top' | 'bottom' | 'left' | 'right';
        container?: HTMLElement;
    };

    // Path interpolation (v1.0.0). Default 'linear'. Per-series override
    // via SeriesConfig.interpolation. Decimated branch ignores this.
    interpolation?: 'linear' | 'step' | 'step-after' | 'step-before'
                  | 'step-mid' | 'monotone' | 'catmull-rom';

    // Marker dots at each sample point (v1.0.0). `true` for circle defaults.
    // `everyN` thins markers for dense series. Suppressed in decimated mode.
    markers?: boolean | {
        shape?: 'circle' | 'square' | 'triangle' | 'diamond';
        size?: number;          // default 5
        fill?: string;          // defaults to series color
        stroke?: string;        // default '#ffffff'
        strokeWidth?: number;   // default 1
        everyN?: number;        // default 1
    };

    // Frame scheduler. Default rAF in browser, synchronous in Node (for
    // headless tests). Pass `queueMicrotask` for coalesced headless benches.
    schedule?: (fn: () => void) => void;
}

interface SeriesConfig {
    name?: string;
    data: Row[] | (() => Row[]) | { xs: Float32Array; ys: Float32Array };
    color?: string;
    lineWidth?: number;
    interpolation?: InterpolationMode;       // per-series override
    markers?: boolean | MarkerConfig;         // per-series override
}

interface Chart {
    mount(target: HTMLElement | HTMLCanvasElement): Chart;
    unmount(): void;
    exportPNG(opts?: { mimeType?: string; quality?: number }): string;
    redraw(): void;

    // v1.0.0-alpha.1: crosshair / tooltip control.
    moveCrosshair(canvasX: number, canvasY: number): void;
    hideCrosshair(): void;

    // v1.0.0-alpha.3: series visibility control.
    setSeriesVisible(idx: number, visible: boolean): void;

    // v1.0.0-beta.0: theme reactivity.
    refreshTheme(): void;                    // re-resolve CSS-var colors + redraw

    readonly scene: Scene | null;          // lite-scene instance
    readonly canvas: HTMLCanvasElement | null;
    readonly xScale: Scale;
    readonly yScale: Scale;
    readonly xScaleType: 'linear' | 'time';
    plotBounds: Signal<number>;            // version counter; read to subscribe
    crosshair: Signal<{                     // live crosshair state; subscribe for sync small-multiples
        visible: boolean;
        snapIdx: number;                    // -1 if hidden
        snapDomainX: number;
        snapPixelX: number;
        mousePixelY: number;
    }>;
    seriesVisibility: Signal<boolean>[];   // one per series; write to toggle
    legend: HTMLElement | null;             // null if legend disabled or bare-canvas mount
}

interface Scale {
    type: 'linear' | 'time';
    dMin: number; dMax: number;
    rMin: number; rMax: number;
    map(value: number): number;            // domain -> pixel
    invert(pixel: number): number;         // pixel -> domain
}
```

## Static-or-signal acceptance

Every config value that could plausibly be reactive accepts both forms.
Internally lite-charts wraps statics in constant accessors via a `asAccessor`
helper, so the engine only ever calls functions. Zero overhead for static
config; full reactivity for signal config:

```js
const w = signal(800);
const chart = createLineChart({ data, width: w, height: 400 });  // mixed
w.set(1200);  // triggers resize + rescale + redraw automatically
```

The donut `centerLabel.text` and `centerLabel.subLabel` follow the same rule --
pass a string for a static label or a `() => string` / signal for a reactive one
(see "Donut center label" below).

## Donut center label (v1.5.0)

`createDonutChart` accepts `centerLabel` -- a number rendered in the hole as a
`pointer-events:none` DOM overlay (NOT canvas text), so it resizes itself:

```js
const data = signal([{label:'Search', value:4200}, {label:'Direct', value:2800}]);
createDonutChart({
  data, innerRadius: 0.55,
  centerLabel: {
    text: () => data().reduce((s, d) => s + d.value, 0).toLocaleString(),
    subLabel: 'Total',
  },
});
```

- Config: `boolean | string | (() => string) | { text, format, subLabel, color,
  font, minFontSize, maxFontSize }`. `centerLabel: true` defaults `format` to the
  total of visible slices; a string / accessor is shorthand for `{ text }`.
- Font size is owned by CSS: the overlay is fixed at
  `font-size: clamp(var(--cl-min), calc(var(--cl-fit) / var(--cl-digits)),
  var(--cl-max))`. On data/resize only (sub-Hz) the chart writes `--cl-fit` (hole
  radius), `--cl-digits` (label length), `--cl-min`/`--cl-max` (floor/cap). More
  digits shrink the number; it tracks resize; zero per-frame JS, no `measureText`.
- Fail-closed: throws at construction if there is no hole (a pie, or resolved
  `innerRadius` 0), and if `minFontSize > maxFontSize`.
- `chart.exportSVG()` emits an equivalent centered `<text>` (same fit formula).
  `chart.centerLabel` exposes the overlay element (null when not configured).
- Zero hot-path cost: the overlay is a DOM sibling of the canvas, never a scene
  node, so the per-frame slice draw is untouched; the `line`/`bar`/`heatmap`
  bundles never pull it in.

## Data shape conventions

Two accepted forms:

1. **AoS (most ergonomic)**: array of row objects.
   ```js
   data: [{ x: 0, y: 1 }, { x: 1, y: 4 }, ...]
   ```
   Internally extracted to SoA `Float32Array` slabs once per data update.

2. **SoA (zero-copy fast path)**: `{ xs: Float32Array, ys: Float32Array }`.
   ```js
   const xs = new Float32Array(N), ys = new Float32Array(N);
   // ... fill ...
   data: { xs, ys }
   ```
   The chart references the buffers directly. Use this when you're already
   producing typed-array data (audio, telemetry, sensor streams, WebGL
   pipelines, etc.).

Multiple series can mix forms.

## Architecture invariants

- **One scene per chart.** `mount` creates a `lite-scene` over the canvas.
  All axes, lines, ticks, labels are scene nodes.
- **Series state is pre-allocated and grown on demand.** Each series has a
  pair of `Float32Array` slabs (`xs`, `ys`, `pxs`, `pys`) plus decimation
  working buffers. Slabs grow by power-of-two doubling; never shrink.
- **The decimation kernel was lifted from `@zakkster/lite-canvas-graph`.**
  Per-column min/max envelope for `n > 2 * plotWidth`. Preserves spike
  visibility. Allocation-free; writes into caller-owned buffers.
- **Two render paths, selected per-draw**: direct polyline for sparse data
  (`n <= 2 * plotWidth`), decimated envelope for dense data. NaN samples
  break the polyline in direct mode and are skipped in decimated mode.
- **Three effects per chart, set up at `mount` time**:
  1. Size/plot-bounds effect (tracks `widthAcc`, `heightAcc`)
  2. Data/scale effect (tracks each series' `dataAccessor` + `plotBoundsSignal`)
  3. Dirty-bridge effect (tracks `scaleVersion` + `plotBoundsSignal`, calls
     `scene.markDirty`)
- **Plus two axis effects** (X and Y), tracking `scaleVersion` and rebuilding
  tick positions from the live scale via `lite-axis.linearTicks` /
  `timeTicks` and `thinLabels`.
- **The line series itself is a `path` node** with a raw draw function. The
  draw closure reads `state.pxs/pys` and color/lineWidth refs directly;
  zero allocation per frame.

## Performance characteristics

Measured at N=100,000 points, canvas 1600x800, Node 22 (CPU only -- mock
canvas):

- Full update cycle (data.set -> draw): **p50 1.39 ms, p95 4.66 ms**
- Decimation kernel alone: **p50 0.52 ms, p95 0.56 ms**
- Draw alone (cached): **p50 0.48 ms, p95 0.58 ms**
- Steady-state heap delta: **~270 bytes/cycle** (target <100; gap is
  niceYDomain tuple + axis label strings + queueMicrotask Promise; v1.0.1
  closes)

Both 60fps (16.67 ms) and 120fps (8.33 ms) budgets fit on the CPU side.
Real GPU paint is additional; browser bench comes in v1.0.1.

## Testing

```
npm test     # 43 deterministic tests via node:test, --expose-gc
npm run bench  # 100k-point latency + allocation report
```

Tests use a recording mock canvas context (`test/harness.js`) that captures
every method call and property assignment into a flat `calls` array. Tests
assert on the call sequence (what was drawn, with what state) so no real
canvas is needed. Bench mode supports `ctx.recordingEnabled = false` to
avoid heap blowup over many frames.

## Common patterns

### Live streaming with a ring buffer

```js
const xs = new Float32Array(1024), ys = new Float32Array(1024);
const data = signal({ xs, ys });
const chart = createLineChart({ data, width: 800, height: 200 });
chart.mount(el);

// In the data source -- writes mutate xs/ys in place; signal.set on the
// same object reference re-extracts and re-projects.
const newDataTick = (newY) => {
    // ... shift the ring, write newY at the head ...
    data.set({ xs, ys });  // forces effect re-fire
};
```

### Multi-series with mixed forms

```js
createLineChart({
    series: [
        { name: 'cpu', data: cpuRows, x: 't', y: 'pct', color: 'red' },
        { name: 'mem', data: { xs: memXs, ys: memYs }, color: 'blue' },
    ],
});
```

### Locked x-domain (for synchronized small multiples)

```js
const sharedX = signal([Date.now() - 3600_000, Date.now()]);
createLineChart({
    data: series1,
    xScale: { type: 'time', domain: untrack(sharedX) },
    // Pass a computed for live sync:
    // xScale: { type: 'time', domain: sharedX() },
});
```

## Gotchas

- **`data: { xs, ys }` is reference-tracked.** The signal compares by
  identity. Mutating the buffers in place and calling `signal.set(sameRef)`
  works -- lite-signal's default `equals` is `Object.is`, which is false
  for `set(x)` vs prior `x` only if you... wait, `Object.is(x, x)` is
  true. So passing the same reference will NOT trigger. Either swap to a
  new wrapper object `signal.set({xs, ys})` (one alloc) or use
  `signal.update(() => ({xs, ys}))`. Future v1.1: add an opt-in
  "rebroadcast" flag to skip the equality check.
- **`exportPNG` requires a real HTMLCanvasElement.** Throws on mock canvases.
- **`exportPNG` does NOT include the donut `centerLabel`.** PNG export is a
  `canvas.toDataURL`, and the center label is a DOM overlay, not a canvas pixel.
  Use `exportSVG` (which emits an equivalent `<text>`) if you need the label in
  an exported image. Intentional.
- **A donut `centerLabel` requires mounting into a DOM element with a parent**
  (so the overlay has a host to interpose). Mounting onto a bare detached canvas
  throws; a plain donut without `centerLabel` mounts anywhere as before.
- **Mount target may be either an element (canvas created inside) or a
  canvas itself.** Test mocks duck-type via `getContext`.
- **In Node, the default schedule is synchronous.** This is correct for
  tests but causes lite-scene to skip draw coalescing -- if you're driving
  many `node.set()` calls per signal write, use
  `schedule: (fn) => queueMicrotask(fn)`. The bench documents this clearly.

## Release history (shipped)

- v1.0.0-beta.0 - beta.3: line + area polish (interp, markers, theme,
  gridlines, zero-alloc crosshair, DPR fix)
- v1.0.0 alpha.0: architectural refactor.
  `_createChartImpl(config, renderKind)` extracted into
  `createBaseAxisChart(config, renderer)` + per-chart renderer objects
  (LINE_RENDERER, AREA_RENDERER, BAR_RENDERER). 22 renderKind branches
  eliminated. Polymorphic dispatch via renderer interface:
  buildXAccessor, createXScale, extractData, updateXScale, buildXAxis,
  makeDrawFn, hitTest, lookupRow, formatTooltipHeader. `rendererCtx`
  singleton (xScale, yScale, opts, categoriesRef) mutated in place --
  preserves zero-alloc on hot path.
- v1.0.0 alpha.1: pie + donut chart family. New `createBasePolarChart`
  kernel -- completely independent from `createBaseAxisChart`. Polar
  state struct: parallel arrays for values (Float32), labels (string[]),
  colors, visibility (Uint8), startAngles (Float64 -- Float32 widens
  PI/2 enough that exact-boundary hits land in wrong slice), arcAngles
  (Float64). `extractSliceData` normalizes array-of-objects, parallel-
  arrays, or plain number arrays. `computeSliceGeometry` centers in
  plot rect with configurable inner radius. `sliceHitTest` is O(n)
  atan2 + linear scan inside ring (n typically 3-12). `makeSliceDrawFn`
  renders wedge (pie) or arc-ring (donut) per slice; hovered slice
  expands 4 px. Pie and donut share SLICE_RENDERER; only innerRadius
  default differs (0 vs 0.5).
- v1.0.0 alpha.2: slice colour resolution bug fix (raw CSS-var leaked
  into canvas fillStyle); demo gets ResizeObserver-backed responsive
  sizing.
- v1.0.0 alpha.3: createBubbleChart on the axis kernel. New
  BUBBLE_RENDERER. Each point becomes a circle with AREA proportional
  to a third dimension via sqrt scale (default; linear available).
  Pixel radii computed at extract time:
  r = sqrt(rMin^2 + t*(rMax^2 - rMin^2)). New seriesState fields `rs`
  (raw sizes) and `prs` (pixel radii) -- both null on non-bubble
  series, zero extra memory. Hit-test signature on the axis kernel
  extended from (canvasX, primary, xScale, ctx) to (canvasX, canvasY,
  primary, xScale, ctx) -- line/area/bar tests ignore canvasY; bubble
  uses both for circle-containment with smallest-on-top tie-breaking
  on overlap.
- v1.0.0 alpha.4: createRadarChart on a third independent kernel.
  Multi-axis polygon layout: N axes (min 3, typical 5-8) spoked from a
  shared center; each series is a polygon connecting one value-per-axis
  vertex. `computeRadarGeometry` precomputes cos/sin per axis into
  Float64 tables -- polygons, grid rings, and spokes all share them,
  zero per-frame trig. `radarHitTest` is nearest-vertex within 12 px
  across visible series. Spoke labels auto-align based on angular
  position. Three drawing layers (grid -> polygons -> spokes+labels) as
  separate scene nodes for natural z-ordering.
- v1.0.0: kernel-side auto-resize. `_wireAutoSize` shared helper; omit
  width / height from config and the chart observes its container via
  ResizeObserver. Three modes per dimension: explicit static, explicit
  reactive (signal/fn), or implicit (auto-observe). Synchronous
  initial read avoids size pop; rAF-throttled updates coalesce burst
  events. Falls back gracefully (keeps default size) when
  ResizeObserver is absent. 182 tests, full tree-shake verification.
- **v1.1.0: bar layout polish.** Stacked bars via new
  `postExtract(states, ctx)` renderer hook -- the kernel calls it
  after the per-series extract loop, bar's hook fills per-series
  `state.stackBottoms` / `state.stackTops` (Float32Arrays, lazy-
  allocated via ensureFloat32) with a visibility-aware cumulative
  accumulator in declaration order; the kernel then re-aggregates
  y-domain to pick up the total stack height. Hidden series excluded
  from the stack; surviving segments snap down on legend toggle.
  Negative values clamp to 0 (diverging stacks deferred to a future
  cut). Rounded corners on the end opposite the baseline (top for
  positive bars, bottom for negative) via native `ctx.roundRect`
  where available + hand-traced `arcTo` fallback for older Safari;
  radii capped at min(w,h)/2. Per-bar hover tint as a CSS-color
  overlay keyed on the chart's `crosshairDataRef.snapIdx`; default
  low-alpha white works against any series color without color
  parsing, opt out with `hoverTint: false`. All three opt-in;
  defaults match v1.0.0 exactly. Bar bundle 25 KB (+1.6 KB);
  line/area/bubble bundles +~300 bytes for the kernel's null-check
  on postExtract; pie/donut/radar unchanged. Three kernels still
  strictly independent -- verified. 196 tests.
- **v1.2.0-alpha.0: spatial-index foundation.** Pluggable
  nearest-neighbor index for O(log n) hit-test on dense point clouds
  (bubble first; scatter + heatmap will ride the same interface in
  alpha.1+). Public contract on `Charts.d.ts`:
  `SpatialIndexFactory = (pxs, pys, n) -> SpatialIndex` where the
  index exposes `findNearest(qx, qy, k, maxDistSq, outIndices,
  outDistSq) -> count` (caller-owned output buffers; zero alloc per
  query) and `dispose()`. `@zakkster/lite-delaunay` is the intended
  default (sweepline Delaunay -> half-edge mesh -> Voronoi-dual walk
  for the cursor's cell) but optional -- k-d tree, uniform-grid, or
  any custom impl works equally well. lite-charts adds it as an
  optional peer dep via `peerDependenciesMeta.optional`. New
  `BUBBLE_RENDERER` config: `spatialIndex: factory` and
  `spatialIndexThreshold` (default 1000). Below threshold the v1.0.0
  linear scan stays the path. Index is lazy-built on the first hit-
  test after extract, cached across queries, disposed on data /
  scale change (extract calls `_disposeSpatialIndex`) AND on chart
  unmount (via new `renderer.cleanup(states)` hook on the axis
  kernel, symmetric with v1.1.0's `postExtract`). `k > 1` matters
  for bubble: overlapping discs mean the nearest CENTER may not be
  the one whose disc contains the cursor; the renderer asks for
  `K = 8` candidates and post-filters by disc containment +
  smallest-r tie-break, preserving v1.0.0 "visually-topmost wins on
  overlap" semantics. Cached `state.prMaxSq` (max pixel-radius
  squared) gives the index a tight maxDistSq upper bound.
  `state._hitIndices` (Int32Array(8)) and `state._hitDistSq`
  (Float32Array(8)) are stable refs that the index writes into.
  Bubble bundle ~22 KB -> ~23 KB. Line / area / bar / pie / donut /
  radar unchanged. 8 new tests. 204 total.
- **v1.2.0-alpha.1: createScatterChart.** New `SCATTER_RENDERER` on
  the axis kernel. Eighth chart type ships. Bubble's simpler sibling:
  no size dimension, every marker the same pixel radius
  (`markerSize`, default 4), hit-test snaps to nearest point within
  `hitTolerance` disc (default `markerSize + 4`). Reuses the
  spatial-index foundation from alpha.0 with `k = 1` (no overlap
  concerns). `_extractScatterData` disposes any existing spatial
  index per-extract so the index rebuilds lazily on data / scale
  change. `_scatterCleanup` symmetric with bubble's: disposes
  indices on unmount. Scatter bundle ~24 KB. Adds nothing to other
  bundles (verified). 6 new tests. 210 total.
- **v1.2.0-alpha.2: multi-series bubble + per-point color +
  global size domain.** `BUBBLE_RENDERER` gains a `postExtract` hook
  (`_bubblePostExtract`) that computes a GLOBAL size domain across
  visible series and re-runs `computeBubbleRadii` on every state.
  Single-series charts short-circuit -- the v1.0.0 fast path stays
  in effect when only one series is visible. Per-series state gets
  `state._stateIdx = i` at construction so the bubble's `lookupRow`
  can tell which series got hit and scope the tooltip to that
  series. Crosshair state gains `snapSeriesIdx` (default -1 --
  non-bubble charts never set it). `_bubbleHitTest` iterates
  `ctx.seriesStates` rather than checking only `primary`. Each
  visible series' bubbles get tested (linear scan or spatial index,
  per its threshold). Returns `snapSeriesIdx` along with `snapIdx`.
  `_initBubbleOpts` gains `colorKey` (string / number / fn). The
  accessor uses `buildRawAccessor` (not `buildAccessor`) so color
  strings like `'#ff0000'` are not `+v`-coerced to NaN.
  `extractBubbleData` extracts per-point colors into `state.cs`
  (plain string Array, lazy-allocated). Colors resolve once via
  `resolveColor` at extract time -- CSS-var values like
  `'--c-emerald'` become concrete strings the draw fn writes to
  `ctx.fillStyle` directly. Bubble draw fn picks `state.cs[i]` per
  row when set, falling back to the series fill otherwise. Zero
  hot-path cost when `colorKey` is unset. Bubble bundle ~23 KB ->
  ~24 KB. Test infra bumped lite-signal default registry to
  `maxNodes: 32768` for 200+ chart-creations across the suite. 9
  new tests. 219 total.
- **v1.2.0-alpha.3: createHeatmap + fourth kernel.**
  New `createBaseGridChart(config, renderer)` kernel. Strictly
  independent from axis / polar / radar kernels -- no cross-kernel
  imports either direction. Heatmap bundle is 10.5 KB minified --
  the smallest of the nine -- because the grid kernel has none of
  the axes / interpolation / decimation / markers / scale-math /
  multi-series weight of the axis kernel. Two band scales (x + y)
  reuse `makeBandScale` math; the y band scale uses the same
  +y-down convention so `yBand.leftEdge(0)` is the topmost cell.
  Cell storage: flat `Float32Array` indexed `yIdx * nx + xIdx`;
  `Uint8Array` `presentMask` for sparse data (missing cells render
  empty, hit-test returns null for them). Per-cell colors
  precomputed at extract into `state.cellColors: string[]` so the
  draw loop is `fillStyle = cellColors[i]; fillRect(...)` --
  zero alloc per cell. Default ramp is linear RGB interpolation
  between two endpoint hex colors. The `colorFn(v, vMin, vMax) ->
  css` config overrides entirely for OKLCH ramps, quantile binning,
  diverging schemes. Hit-test is O(1) -- one `xBand.invert` + one
  `yBand.invert` + a presence-mask check. `chart.hover` is a
  signal-style reactive accessor with `.peek()` escape hatch.
  Mouse events on canvas drive `moveHover` / `hideHover`
  automatically. Axis labels render inline (no lite-axis dep for
  the grid kernel since categories are arbitrary strings). 12 new
  tests. 231 total.
- **v1.2.0: destroy() + heatmap polish.**
  **chart.destroy() on all four kernels.** Each kernel tracks every
  signal it creates at construction time in a per-instance
  `_ownedSignals` array via a small `_own(s)` helper; `destroy()`
  calls `unmount()` first if mounted, then iterates the array and
  calls lite-signal's `dispose()` on each. The visibility-growth
  paths in polar (`ensureVisibilitySignals`) and radar
  (`ensureSeriesSlots`) push new signals through `_own` too so the
  array stays in sync as series counts change. Verified zero
  residue across 30 mount+destroy cycles on every kernel.
  Idempotent. Works before `mount()` too (signals exist before
  mount, so they need cleanup even if the chart was never
  displayed). **Heatmap quantile binning** (`colorScale: 'quantile'`,
  `colorBins` default 5, clamp [2, 20]): collect present values,
  sort, place N-1 boundaries at the i/N percentiles, pre-compute
  one color per bin from the same lo/hi ramp; per-cell assignment
  is a linear scan through the boundaries (zero alloc on the
  per-cell path). Outliers no longer dominate the ramp.
  **Heatmap row + column highlights**: fill stripes the full plot
  width (row) and full plot height (column) at the band width of
  the hovered cell, drawn before the cell stroke. Both default on,
  independently disable-able via `rowHighlight: false` /
  `columnHighlight: false`. Stripe color
  (`rowColumnHighlightFill`, default `rgba(0,0,0,0.10)`) resolved
  at mount so CSS-vars work. **Auto-contrast value labels**:
  `valueLabelColor` defaults to `'auto'` for `showValues: true`.
  Per-cell NTSC luminance (`0.299R + 0.587G + 0.114B`) picks
  `#000000` / `#ffffff`. Computed at extract time alongside the
  cell color into `state.cellLabelColors` (no extra pass).
  `_parseRGBLike` handles `rgb(...)` and hex; named / oklch / rgba
  fall through to `#ffffff`. Explicit `valueLabelColor` skips the
  per-cell allocation entirely. Helpers added:
  `_pickContrastColor`, `_parseRGBLike`. Helper removed:
  `_lerpRGBString` (linear / quantile paths now inline the lerp
  to keep R/G/B integers in scope for luminance). 14 new tests.
  245 total.
- **v1.3.0: chart.exportSVG() across all four kernels.**
  Every chart now returns a static SVG of its current frame via
  `chart.exportSVG(opts?)`. Implementation: a Canvas2D-shaped shim
  (`_SVGRenderingContext2D`, ~270 LOC in Charts.js) accumulates SVG
  markup instead of issuing pixel ops. State stack snapshots CTM,
  fillStyle, strokeStyle, lineWidth, lineCap, lineJoin, lineDash,
  globalAlpha, font, textAlign, textBaseline, clipPathId. Method
  coverage: save/restore; translate/rotate/scale/setTransform/
  resetTransform; beginPath/closePath/moveTo/lineTo/bezierCurveTo/
  quadraticCurveTo/rect/arc/arcTo/roundRect; stroke/fill (emit
  `<path d>`); fillRect/strokeRect (emit `<rect>` via _axisAligned
  check, falls through to path for rotated cases); fillText/
  strokeText (emit `<text>` with text-anchor + dominant-baseline
  derived from canvas textAlign + textBaseline); setLineDash/
  getLineDash; clip() emits `<clipPath>` def + url() refs.
  Unsupported (drawImage, gradients, shadows) are silent no-ops --
  none of the v1.3.0 chart code uses them.
  **_drawNodeToSVG / _drawSelfToSVG** walker mirrors lite-scene's
  drawNode/drawSelf structurally, walking `scene.root` recursively
  through the shim. Handles every node kind: rect (radius +
  roundRect), circle, line, text, path (delegates to the node's
  custom _draw callback), group with optional _clip function.
  **_exportSceneToSVG(scene, width, height, background)** is the
  shared entry point each kernel's `chart.exportSVG()` calls with
  its current width/height signals and resolved background.
  **SVGExportOptions**: `{ background?: string | null }` --
  defaults to construction-time `config.background`. Chart must
  be mounted; mock canvases work too (SVG export doesn't read
  pixel data). Text-width estimation is approximate (~0.55 em
  per char). **Bug fix**: pre-existing typo at Charts.js line
  1329 -- band-axis builder passed `anchor: 'center'` to a
  lite-scene textNode that expects `align:`. The wrong key was
  silently dropped, leaving `_align` at its default `'left'`.
  Single-character labels masked it; multi-character names were
  offset right by half a glyph width. Fix is one-key; both canvas
  and SVG output benefit. **Tests**: 14 new under `chart.exportSVG()`
  -- valid envelope per chart type, rounded-corner arcs on bars,
  fixed text-anchor=middle on bar labels (regression guard for
  the band-axis fix), XML escaping of label text, `background`
  option emits a background rect, throws when unmounted, throws
  after destroy. 259 total.
  **Types**: `SVGExportOptions` declared; `Chart.exportSVG`,
  `RadarChart.exportSVG`, `PolarChart.exportSVG` all added.
  `RadarChart` and `PolarChart` also picked up the v1.2.0
  `destroy()` that was missing from their specialized interfaces.
  **Bundle deltas**: every chart picks up ~8.9 KB of SVG
  infrastructure. All-nine went from 72.8 KB to ~82.4 KB (only
  ~9.6 KB delta because the SVG helpers are shared module-level
  functions deduplicated by the bundler). Cross-
  kernel isolation verified clean (the SVG helpers are shared
  module-level functions, not kernel-specific).
- **v1.4.0-alpha.0: log scale on the y-axis.**
  Opt in with `yScale: { type: 'log' }` on any axis-kernel chart
  (line, area, bar, bubble, scatter). NEW `makeLogScale()` +
  `updateLogScale(s, dMin, dMax, rMin, rMax)` -- same shape as
  `makeLinearScale` (`type`, `dMin/dMax/rMin/rMax`, cached
  `_slope/_intercept/_invSlope`) but `map(v)` does
  `Math.log(v) * slope + intercept` and `invert(px)` does
  `Math.exp((px - intercept) * invSlope)`. The scale object also
  caches `_logDMin` / `_logDMax` in case future tick or projection
  code needs them; the v1.4.0-alpha.0 map/invert paths don't read
  them. Tick generation routes through `lite-axis`'s already-shipped
  `logTicks(min, max, target, out, minor=false)` -- decade boundaries
  (1, 10, 100, ...) with the major-only mode for alpha.0; the 2x/5x
  minor sub-tick mode is parked for a later cut (likely exposed as
  `tickSubdivisions: 'major' | 'all'`). `map(v <= 0)` returns NaN
  explicitly so draw fns can break the segment (line/area) or skip
  the marker (bubble/scatter); without this, `Math.log(-x)` would
  propagate NaN through downstream draw code anyway, but explicit is
  clearer for callers debugging "why is my segment missing".
  `updateLogScale` safety-clamps non-positive `dMin` to `1e-10` and
  reverses swapped bounds (`dMax < dMin`). Polymorphic `s.map()` in
  tick projection (was inlined `tickBuf[i] * slope + intercept` in
  both the main axis builder and the grid-extras builder) handles
  linear and log without parallel code paths -- ~12 method calls per
  axis update at sub-Hz rate, perf-irrelevant. Hot draw paths
  (per-frame point projection) remain untouched. `_testHelpers` now
  exports `makeLogScale` + `updateLogScale` for scale-math unit
  tests. Types: `yScale.type` accepts `'linear' | 'log'` (was
  `'linear'` only); the existing `domain`, `nice`, `zero` options
  remain. Tests: 13 new under `log scale (v1.4.0-alpha.0)` --
  7 math tests (decade boundaries, round-trip invert, NaN for
  non-positive, dMin clamp, degenerate dMin===dMax, swapped bounds,
  same shape as linear) + 6 end-to-end (line chart, scatter chart,
  default-linear back-compat, scale type survives data update, SVG
  export with log scale, decade-boundary labels). 272 total.
  Bundle deltas: ~600 bytes per axis-kernel chart for the scale
  builders + tick switch + logTicks import; grid kernel (heatmap)
  untouched since it uses band scales on both axes and doesn't pull
  the linear/log code. Caveats worth knowing: log + bar is rendered
  but conventionally nonsensical (bars are magnitude-from-zero;
  log has no meaningful zero); log on the x-axis isn't wired yet
  (plumbing is symmetric; small follow-up).
- **v1.4.0-alpha.1: audit-fix-only release.**
  Four allocation traps inherited from v1.2-1.3 code surfaced in a
  bare-metal review and are fixed here without any public API
  change. The v1.4 interaction-primitives work shifts one alpha slot
  forward (alpha.2 = pan + zoom, alpha.3 = brushing).
  (1) **Heatmap quantile gather/sort.** Was
  `const present = []; .push(state.cells[i]); .sort((a,b) => a-b)`
  in `_computeGridColors` -- on a 200x200 dense heatmap that's a
  40k-element standard JS Array allocated and thrown away per data
  update. Fixed: pool a `Float32Array` on
  `state.presentSorted` (new field on `_makeGridState`); pack
  present values into a `[0, nPresent)` prefix; sort an in-place
  `presentSorted.subarray(0, nPresent)` view via
  `Float32Array.prototype.sort()` -- which without args sorts
  numerically and allocates nothing. Pool grows monotonically with
  chart size; steady-state is zero-alloc.
  (2) **`_parseRGBLike` per-cell split.** When `colorFn` returned an
  `rgb(...)` string and `valueLabelColor === 'auto'`, parse called
  `css.slice(open+1, close).split(',')` per cell at extract time.
  10k cells = 10k Arrays + 30k substring objects, allocated and
  tossed every update. Fixed: `indexOf` scan finds the two commas
  inside the parens; three substring slices total (V8 may
  sliced-string them; even materialized they're 3-4 chars each), no
  intermediate array.
  (3) **`charBufToString` rope walk.** Built the label string via
  `let s = ''; for (...) s += String.fromCharCode(buf[i])`. The `+=`
  inside a loop allocates N intermediate strings as V8 walks the
  rope -- ~200 string allocations per axis update for an axis with
  20 ticks at 10 chars each. Fixed:
  `String.fromCharCode.apply(null, buf.subarray(0, n))` -- one call,
  one allocation. `buf.subarray()` is a zero-alloc view onto the
  existing Uint8Array; arg-count limit (~64k on V8) is far above
  TICK_BUF_SIZE.
  (4) **SVG-export rope-string limit.** The most consequential.
  `_SVGRenderingContext2D` accumulated path commands via
  `this._currentPath += chunk` for every moveTo / lineTo / arc /
  etc. At 100k+ points the rope walk on the `<path d="...">`
  attribute read in stroke()/fill() could hit `RangeError: Invalid
  string length` or stall the main thread for seconds during the
  rope flatten. Fixed: every path command pushes into
  `this._pathChunks` (array); `_pathD()` does
  `this._pathChunks.join('')` exactly once when stroke/fill/clip
  needs the d-attribute. Arrays grow amortized O(1); join flattens
  in one allocation. `beginPath()` truncates via
  `this._pathChunks.length = 0` (in-place, no realloc).
  `fillRect`/`strokeRect` rotated-fallback path swaps chunks arrays
  (the saved one is a small temporary allocation; this branch is
  rare since chart code only rotates pie slices + radar polygons,
  not rects). Stress-test: 50,000-point scatter chart now exports to
  a 5.2 MB SVG with 50,021 path elements in 165 ms; pre-alpha.1
  this would have either crashed with RangeError or stalled the
  main thread for seconds.
  Tests: 8 new under `audit-fix regressions (v1.4.0-alpha.1)` --
  10k-point line export produces valid SVG; path d-attribute starts
  with `M<num>` and contains `L<num>` (no rope-flatten artifacts);
  two consecutive exports produce byte-identical output (catches
  begin/end path bookkeeping leaks); pie rotated-rect fallback
  still works; 50x50 quantile-binned heatmap doesn't throw;
  quantile output stable on a fixed dataset (Float32Array sort
  numerically equivalent to JS Array sort); auto-label color
  survives custom colorFn returning `rgb(...)`; axis labels render
  correctly after the charBufToString rewrite. 280 total.
  Bench unchanged: 166 bytes/cycle (within natural variance of the
  161 alpha.0 baseline). All four fixes target paths that fire on
  data-update or export, not on the per-frame draw. Bundles: line
  +0.1 KB, bar +0.2 KB, scatter +0.1 KB, heatmap +0.4 KB vs
  alpha.0 (the heatmap delta is the new `presentSorted: null`
  field on grid state plus chunk-style comments). Audit credit:
  user-provided bare-metal review; the fixes match the recommended
  patterns exactly. Every fix has a code comment naming the trap
  it closes so future readers don't accidentally reintroduce the
  pattern.
- **v1.4.0-alpha.2: pan + zoom on axis-kernel charts.**
  Opt in via `pan: true` and/or `zoom: true` on any axis-kernel
  chart (line, area, bubble, scatter; bar inherits typing but
  band-axis isn't ideal). Either flag allocates the view signal
  and attaches the listener cluster; neither set = no view, no
  listeners, zero cost. Public API: `chart.view` reactive accessor
  (`chart.view()` reads + tracks, `.peek()` reads untracked,
  `.set(v)` writes, `.reset()` clears); `chart.setView(v)` and
  `chart.resetView()` are imperative aliases. View shape is
  `{ xMin, xMax, yMin, yMax }` with any field nullable for "fall
  back to data domain on that axis" -- intentionally symmetric
  with `lite-camera-max`'s camera signal so the same value drops
  into a future lite-gl `project()` function unchanged.
  Configuration: `panBounds: 'data' | 'free'` (default 'data'
  clamps to data domain; 'free' allows past), `zoomMin` / `zoomMax`
  as visible-span / data-span ratio (defaults 0.01 / 1000),
  `zoomStep` wheel ratio per tick (default 1.15, clamped >= 1.001).
  Interaction model: cursor-anchor convention (d3-zoom / Plotly /
  Google Maps) -- data point under cursor at gesture start stays
  under cursor. Drag right -> view shifts LEFT in data space (you
  see more leftward data); drag up -> view shifts DOWN in data
  space (content rolls up with cursor; y-axis labels effectively
  scroll down). pointer events (pointerdown/move/up/cancel/leave)
  used uniformly so pen, touch, mouse all work; setPointerCapture
  used when available so a drag escaping the canvas still completes.
  Wheel registered with `passive: false` + `preventDefault` so
  page-scroll doesn't fight the zoom. Architecture: view-override
  layer sits between data-domain extraction and scale-update calls;
  the existing scale-update effect adds viewSig() as a dependency
  so chart.setView() triggers a full re-project + redraw via
  existing reactive plumbing -- no parallel code path. `_dataDomain`
  is a non-reactive plain-object snapshot populated by the scale-
  update effect every time it runs; listeners read it inside event
  handlers for bounds clamping without touching the reactive graph
  (and only allocated when interactionsEnabled). Math helpers
  `_applyPan(start, dxPx, dyPx, plotW, plotH)`, `_applyZoom(start,
  anchorPx, anchorPy, plotLeft, plotTop, plotW, plotH, zoomX,
  zoomY)`, `_clampToBounds(view, dataDom)` are module-level + pure,
  exported via `_testHelpers` for white-box tests; tree-shaken
  away in builds that don't use pan/zoom (only reachable through
  listener closures, which are only built when interactionsEnabled).
  Crosshair coexists -- pointerdown hides crosshair once; it
  resumes naturally on next mousemove after pointerup. Types:
  `View` and `PanZoomConfig` interfaces added; `LineChartConfig`,
  `BubbleChartConfig`, `ScatterChartConfig` extend `PanZoomConfig`;
  `Chart` interface gains `view`, `setView`, `resetView`. Scope
  limitations: alpha.2 is linear arithmetic on data domain. For
  `yScale: { type: 'log' }` charts the math is technically wrong
  (adds and scales in data space rather than log space) -- chart
  renders, but pan magnitude won't feel right; log-aware path is
  a small follow-up. Polar / radar / heatmap kernels don't get
  pan/zoom (different interaction models). Brushing originally
  scheduled for alpha.2 shifts to alpha.3: modifier-key drag will
  emit `brushSignal` for cross-chart filtering; will coexist with
  pan/zoom (no modifier = pan, shift = brush). Tests: 24 new (10
  math, 5 view-facade + scale-integration, 7 pointer/wheel
  integration with extended mock canvas, 2 reactive flow). 304
  total. Bundles: line +1.2 KB, bar +1.2 KB, bubble +1.2 KB,
  scatter +1.2 KB; heatmap / radar / pie untouched. Bench
  unchanged -- pan/zoom doesn't touch per-frame draw; view
  overrides happen once per scale update (sub-Hz), math helpers
  invoked only on pointer/wheel events. Bundles (actuals): line +3.7
  KB, area +3.9 KB, bar +3.7 KB, bubble +3.9 KB, scatter +3.7 KB vs
  alpha.1 -- the listener cluster + viewFacade + closure-captured
