  math helpers. Heatmap unchanged; pie/donut +0.1 KB, radar +0.2 KB
  (shared module-level code touched). All-nine: 83.1 -> 87.3 KB.
  Cross-kernel isolation verified: heatmap/pie/donut/radar bundles
  contain no `_applyPan` / `_applyZoom` / `_clampToBounds` /
  `viewFacade` strings. Bench unchanged (164.7 bytes/cycle vs alpha.1's
  166 -- noise band, per-frame draw path untouched).
- **v1.4.0-alpha.3: brushing -- final v1.4 alpha.** Opt in
  via `brush: true` on any axis-kernel chart. Shift+drag selects a
  rectangular region; chart emits `BrushSelection { xMin, xMax,
  yMin, yMax, ids }` via `chart.brush` reactive facade (same pattern
  as chart.view: callable for tracked read, `.peek()` for untracked
  read, `.set(v)` for write, `.clear()` for clear; `chart.setBrush`
  and `chart.clearBrush` are imperative aliases; both throw if
  `brush: true` was not in config). `ids` are indices into the
  PRIMARY series (first series in `series[]`, or the single-series
  `data`); freshly allocated each gesture commit (not pooled --
  aliasing across brushes would surprise users; brushing is sub-Hz
  so the allocation is acceptable). Programmatic `setBrush()` leaves
  `ids` as null unless the caller passes them -- the API never
  recomputes ids on imperative set; only gesture-driven brushes
  populate ids. Modifier routing: bare drag = pan (when pan: true),
  shift+drag = brush (when brush: true), wheel = zoom (when
  zoom: true, modifier-agnostic). pointerdown checks `ev.shiftKey`
  and the pan listener returns early when shift is held AND brush is
  enabled, so the same canvas can host all three interactions without
  conflict. Click-to-clear: shift+click with total drag distance
  under 3 px is treated as a click and clears the existing brush
  (matches d3-brush default). Live updates: brushSig updates on
  every pointermove during gesture -- cross-chart linking via
  `effect()` reflects the user's drag in real time; final commit
  fires on pointerup. Visual: translucent rect overlay rendered
  AFTER the crosshair node so it sits on top. Defaults to indigo
  accent fill (`rgba(99, 102, 241, 0.15)`) + dashed accent outline
  (`[4, 4]`, 1px). Override via `brushStyle: { fill, stroke,
  lineDash, lineWidth }`; pass `lineDash: []` for solid outline.
  Math helpers (module-level, pure, exported via _testHelpers):
  `_normalizeBrushRect(px0, py0, px1, py1)` orders a drag rect into
  min/max corners; `_brushPxToData(rect, xScale, yScale)` inverts
  pixel rect to data bounds via scales (y-flipped: pyMin -> yMax,
  pyMax -> yMin); `_computeBrushIds(xs, ys, n, xMin, xMax, yMin,
  yMax)` returns array of indices inside the rect. All three
  tree-shaken away in builds that don't use brush. Brush state
  machine is fully independent of pan's drag state (separate
  active bit, separate start coords); both gestures share the same
  pointer-event family and setPointerCapture flow. Crosshair
  suppression: pointerdown hides crosshair once, resumes on next
  mousemove after pointerup (matches pan). Tests: 16 new (6 math,
  5 facade, 5 integration via extended mock canvas). 320 total.
  Bundles: line +2.9 KB, bar +2.9 KB, bubble +2.8 KB, scatter +2.9 KB
  vs alpha.2; heatmap/pie/radar UNCHANGED -- cross-kernel isolation
  verified (no `_normalizeBrushRect` / `_brushPxToData` /
  `_computeBrushIds` / `brushFacade` strings in those bundles).
  All-nine: 87.3 -> 90.2 KB. Bench unchanged (164.0 vs alpha.2's
  164.7 -- noise band). Types: `BrushSelection`, `BrushStyleConfig`,
  `BrushConfig` interfaces added; `Chart` interface gains `brush`,
  `setBrush`, `clearBrush`; `LineChartConfig`, `BubbleChartConfig`,
  `ScatterChartConfig` extend `BrushConfig` (bar inherits via
  existing Omit chain). Scope (unchanged from alpha.2): axis-kernel
  charts only -- polar/radar/heatmap don't get brushing (different
  interaction models); log-scale charts work but the math is the
  same as alpha.2's pan/zoom -- linear arithmetic on data domain,
  not log-aware. Fixed shift modifier; configurable modifier is a
  follow-up. v1.4 alpha line complete: alpha.0 log scale, alpha.1
  audit fixes, alpha.2 pan + zoom, alpha.3 brushing. Combined
  v1.4.0 release follows -- same code as alpha.3 plus a clean
  release-notes rollup, no further API or behavior changes.

## Capacity (lite-signal arena)

lite-signal's default node-arena capacity is **1024 nodes**. Each
axis-kernel chart uses ~45-60 active nodes (the dominant cost is
the per-axis tick pool: each tick = `lineNode` + `textNode` = 2
scene-node effects, at max 12 ticks per axis = ~24 effects per axis
x 2 axes = ~48). Heatmap uses ~5 nodes (grid kernel renders cells
through a single pathNode per layer). Pie / donut use ~25.

**Default 1024 fits ~15-20 axis-kernel charts.** Dashboards or demos
with more must bump the registry BEFORE constructing any chart:

```js
import { createRegistry, setDefaultRegistry } from '@zakkster/lite-signal';
setDefaultRegistry(createRegistry({ maxNodes: 32768 }));
```

The lite-charts demo (`demo/index.html`) and the test suite both
bump to 32768 for this reason. Bumping after charts are already
constructed doesn't help those charts -- they read the current
default registry at construction time.

**mount / unmount / destroy** (v1.2.0): `unmount()` disposes the
scene and all draw effects but keeps construction-time signals
(`widthAutoSig`, `plotBoundsSignal`, etc.) alive so the chart can
be remounted -- which leaves ~4 nodes residue per cycle.
`chart.destroy()` is the terminal counterpart: calls `unmount()`
first if mounted, then disposes every owned signal. After
`destroy()` the chart cannot be remounted; subsequent `destroy()`
calls are no-ops. Use it for apps that create and destroy many
charts dynamically.

## Forward plan

- v1.4.0 (next; alpha line in progress):
  - v1.4.0-alpha.0: log scale. New `makeLogScale()` alongside the
    existing `makeLinearScale` and `makeBandScale`. `yScale: { type:
    'log' }` (and same for `xScale`). Tick generation routes to
    `lite-axis`'s already-shipped `logTicks` (decade boundaries +
    optional 2x/5x sub-ticks per decade). Non-positive data is
    caller's responsibility; chart draws what it can with any
    positive values present.
  - v1.4.0-alpha.1: pan + zoom. Mouse-drag pans, wheel zooms. Driven
    by a `view` signal carrying `{ xMin, xMax, yMin, yMax }` so
    bounded-history undo/redo is one signal snapshot away. The view
    signal is shape-symmetric with `lite-camera-max`'s camera signal,
    so users can drop a chart's view-signal into a lite-gl `project`
    function unchanged when the companion package lands.
  - v1.4.0-alpha.2: brushing. Modifier-key (shift) drag selects a
    region; emits a `brushSignal` carrying `{ x: [min,max], y:
    [min,max], ids: number[] }` for cross-chart filtering. Coexists
    with pan/zoom -- no modifier pans, shift brushes.
- Companion track -- `@zakkster/lite-charts-gl` (post-v1.4.0):
  separate package built on `@zakkster/lite-gl` (browser-only WebGL2).
  Targets chart types currently bottlenecked by point count.
  v0.1 scope: `createScatterChartGL` (POINT pipeline, 1:1 mapping
  to lite-gl's 8-float-per-point layout), `createBubbleChartGL`
  (same kernel, `size` field becomes the radius attribute), and
  `createDensityChart` (a new tenth chart type for the 100k-1M
  point range where overdraw kills scatter). Spatial-index hit-test
  stays on CPU. Axis ticks stay in a canvas overlay (cheap; GL
  overkill for text). Reuses lite-charts's scale builders, lifecycle
  API, and configuration shape. The split at the package boundary
  keeps lite-charts node-testable end-to-end while letting
  lite-charts-gl own the WebGL2 testing pattern lite-gl
  established (mock-WebGL2-context unit tests + real-GPU
  Playwright). Bench target: 1M scatter points at 60fps with
  signal-driven pan/zoom.
- v1.12.x / v1.13.0 (candidates): overnight session support (close < open
  via midnight-split open intervals -- throws today); holiday-calendar
  convenience over the annotation range primitive; horizontal (top/bottom)
  legend virtualization (throws today); horizontal-bar brush band-axis
  multi-select refinements + a configurable brush modifier; brush ids across
  all visible series (currently primary-series only).
- v2.0.0 (possible): renderer-agnostic kernel refactor (if
  lite-charts-gl proves out, fold the renderer choice into core);
  deeper SSR support.
